newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln sees CIGNA deal adding to earnings.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln sees CIGNA deal adding to earnings.

text.p: Lincoln National Corp Chief Executive Ian Rolland said he expects CIGNA Corp's individual life insurance and annuity business to add $0.21 per share to Lincoln National earnings in 1998.
Rolland, speaking to Reuters in an interview, said he expects the business to add $0.22 per share to earnings in 1999.
Earlier, Lincoln National said it had agreed to acquire CIGNA's individual life insurance and annuity business for $1.4 billion in cash.
Rolland said he does not expect any material charge to 1997 earnings in connection with the acquisition.
With this transaction, Lincoln National, already a powerhouse in the annuity business, would strengthen its presence in the life insurance business, Rolland said.
The deal further underscores Lincoln National's transformation as it gears up to compete in a deregulated financial services industry, Rolland said.
Lincoln National in June agreed to sell its 83.3 percent stake in American States Financial Corp, a property-casualty insurer, to SAFECO Corp, resulting in proceeds of $2.15 billion after tax.
Lincoln, at that time, said it planned to use the proceeds to acquire a life insurance and annuity operation.

Rolland declined to say whether Lincoln National seriously considered any other properties but said CIGNA's business had been at the top of Lincoln National's target list, saying it was an excellent strategic fit.
The CIGNA business would give Lincoln National cross selling opportunities as well as 600 career agents with expertise in the financial planning business, Rolland said.

He said he expects to maintain headquarters for life insurance sales and marketing in Hartford, where the CIGNA business is based, and headquarters for the annuity business and customer service in Fort Wayne, Ind., where Lincoln National is based.
However, he said, he expects to achieve pretax cost savings of $40 million by 1999 and said this will involve some staff reductions.
He declined to estimate how many job cuts might be involved with the transaction.

Rolland said he does not expect Lincoln National to make any additional large-scale acquisitions in the near term, noting that the company has nearly used up the expected proceeds from the American States sale.

In addition to the $1.4 billion the company plans to spend on the CIGNA business, Lincoln National recently agreed to buy a 49 percent stake in a Mexican insurance business for $85 million and plans to use $500 million of the American States proceeds to buy back stock.

He said the company has already spent $180 million of that $500 million. Rolland declined to say how quickly Lincoln National plans to use the remaining $320 million authorized for the stock repurchase program.
Lincoln National may make some small-scale acquisitions in its Delaware Management investment management business, Rolland said.
And, he said, the company may make some additional life insurance acquisitions outside the United States, possibly in the United Kingdom.
But, he said, "assuming the completion of the buyback, we will have effectively redeployed all the assets of American States."
